title: Multicenter, 3-arm, randomized, controlled study on the rapid antidepressant efficacy and safety of hyperthermic baths in depression
summary:
This study has been set up to evaluate the quick antidepressant efficacy and safety of hyperthermic baths in depression.
The participants take 16 baths over 8 weeks. They document their impressions in questionnaires and keep a diary. Several visits at the study site 1x per week in person are followed by some on the telephone. In this course, potential adverse events and changes in standard therapy are being monitored and additional questionnaires completed. After further 2 and 6 weeks resp., follow-up visits take place.
Primary objective of the study is to reduce depression severity (MADRS score after 2 weeks); secondary objective comprises improvement in quality of life regarding health and sleep. Data on co-interventions like physical activity and phytotherapy are being collected as well.
The following hypotheses will be evaluated:
1. Hyperthermic baths plus standard treatment reduce depressive symptoms within 2 weeks, compared with stand-alone standard treatment.
2. Hyperthermic baths plus standard treatment reduce depressive symptoms within 2 weeks, compared with thermoneutral baths plus stand-alone standard treatment.

interventions.name: Hyperthermic baths (HTB) with 2 applications per week + treatment as usual (TAU)
Thermoneutral baths (TNB) with 2 applications per week + treatment as usual (TAU)
Treatment as usual (TAU; drug therapy and/or psychotherapy)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Signed Informed Consent Form (ICF)
•	Outpatients (both male and female) between the age of 18-70 who are receiving treatment as usual or who are off antidepressant therapy for at least 4 weeks prior to baseline
•	confirmed diagnosis of depression (ICD-10 F32/F33 criteria for single or recurrent nonpsychotic depression >2 weeks)
•	MADRS score indicating at least a moderate depression (MADRS ≥ 20)
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute risk of suicide
- Change of antidepressant therapy within <4 weeks prior to baseline or intention to change antidepressant therapy within the next two weeks
- Other mental disorder (i.e. borderline personality disorder, bipolar affective disorder, drug and/or alcohol abuse, schizophrenia, anxiety disorder, psychotic depression)
- Contraindication for hot baths (i.e. open wounds, heat urticaria, varicosis, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, orthostatic dysregulation, pregnancy)
- Severe organic disease (i.e. heart failure)
- Ongoing pension claim
